findings.title: Credential key overwritten with a zod SafeParse result object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result, i.e. `{ success, data }`, not the token itself. That whole object is then written as `key` in `prisma.credential.update`. After the first refresh, every Google Calendar credential is stored as `{success:true,data:{...}}`. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, which breaks the integration for all users, including installs where sync is disabled. Store `key.data` instead.

findings.title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response that callers don't expect
findings.body:
When sync is enabled, the function returns a WHATWG `Response`. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data`, which is undefined on a fetch Response, so `token.access_token` throws.
- Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object; it reads `.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` and persists the Response object as the key.
- Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin expect an axios response and read `.data.error` / `.data.access_token`.

With sync enabled, refresh is broken for all of these apps. The helper should normalize its return value, or callers should handle both shapes.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses bogus computed keys and strips the expiry
findings.body:
`z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]". The schema therefore has a single key named "[object Object]" (the second overrides the first), not a wildcard for numeric expiry fields.

Because `z.object` strips unknown keys, the parsed data only keeps `access_token`; `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and similar fields are dropped. For example, in sync mode Zoom computes `Date.now() + undefined*1000`, which gives NaN, so the stored expiry is corrupt and refresh loops. Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record`, and validate the expiry field explicitly.

findings.title: Placeholder "refresh_token" overwrites real refresh tokens
findings.body: If the provider response lacks a `refresh_token`, the helper sets it to the literal string "refresh_token". Office 365 merges this into the stored credentials with `{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`. Microsoft frequently omits `refresh_token` on refresh, so the user's valid refresh token is replaced with the string "refresh_token". The next refresh then fails permanently. This happens even when sync is disabled.

findings.title: `prisma` used without being imported
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but `@calcom/prisma` is never imported in this file. This is a compile error, or at runtime a ReferenceError that rejects `getClient`, so every Salesforce operation fails.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation and keeps using the old access token
findings.body:
`getClient` now calls the Salesforce token endpoint unconditionally on every service construction, with no expiry check. This adds a network round trip and rate-limit pressure on every booking.

The freshly obtained access token is also discarded: the connection is built with `credentialKey.access_token` (the old value) and `credentialKey.instance_url`. On top of that, the `statusText !== "OK"` check fails over HTTP/2, where `statusText` is empty. The refresh also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it ignores the sync feature entirely.

findings.title: Credential id passed where user id is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` takes a `userId` as its third argument, but Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId`. In sync mode the self-hosted endpoint receives `calcomUserId` set to a credential id, so it returns the wrong user's tokens or none. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

findings.title: appStoreMetadata looked up by slug instead of directory name
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`. The handler indexes it with the DB slug, e.g. `google-calendar`, `zoom`. For most apps the lookup returns undefined and the webhook responds 404 "App not found". Look up by matching `slug` across the values instead.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared non-constant-time; no method check; parse errors give 500s
findings.body:
- The shared secret is compared with `!==`, which is not timing-safe; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
- The handler accepts any HTTP method.
- `schema.parse` throws on a bad body, and `symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` throw on a bad payload or wrong key. These surface as unhandled 500s instead of 400s.

findings.title: Inconsistent app slug sent to sync endpoint
findings.body: Zoom sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, but the app's slug is `zoom`, which is what the credential uses as `appId` and what the webhook expects. A self-hosted sync endpoint keyed by slug will not recognise the Zoom request.

findings.title: Outbound token-sync request carries no authentication
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no secret, signature or header. The self-hoster's endpoint cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com, yet it is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids. The request should include the webhook secret header or an equivalent signature.
